components.name: userTask
components.description: A task that requires human intervention. Users interact with 'user tasks' via a task management system
components.usage: Use this task type when a task in the process flow requires manual action by a user. It typically involves human interaction, such as reviewing a document, approving a request, or entering data.

requiredInputs.name: taskName
requiredInputs.description: Name of the eTask for identification and display purposes

requiredInputs.name: taskDescription
requiredInputs.description: Detailed description of what the user needs to do in this task

requiredInputs.name: sourceSystemName
requiredInputs.description: Source system or process that generated this task

requiredInputs.name: taskPriority
requiredInputs.description: Priority level of the task

requiredInputs.name: taskDeadline
requiredInputs.description: Expected completion date and time for the task in date format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) or  duration (e.g. P{days}DT{hours}H{minutes}M)

requiredInputs.name: maximumActiveTasks
requiredInputs.description: Maximum number of active user tasks allowed to run concurrently

generatedOutputs.name: reasonCode
generatedOutputs.description: Reason code indicating how the task was completed. Useful for determining approval outcomes (e.g., 'APPROVED' vs 'REJECTED') or other completion reasons

generatedOutputs.name: comment
generatedOutputs.description: The comment entered by the user who completed the task

generatedOutputs.name: taskIdentifier
generatedOutputs.description: Unique reference identifier for the completed task instance. Useful for tracking, auditing, or correlating this specific task execution with external systems

components.name: serviceTask
components.description: A task performed by an external software service. Typically a REST call to GET/PUT/POST/DELETE
components.usage: Use service tasks when a task in the process flow can be automated and executed by a software service or application without direct human involvement. It often involves invoking external systems, performing calculations, or executing predefined functions

requiredInputs.name: serviceUrl
requiredInputs.description: Direct HTTP/HTTPS URL of the target service (e.g., https://api.example.com). Use this when the service endpoint is known and accessible via a direct URL

requiredInputs.name: uriPath
requiredInputs.description: Specific URI path to append to the location identifier

requiredInputs.name: httpMethod
requiredInputs.description: HTTP Method of the request to be invoked on the REST service called by this task

requiredInputs.name: headers
requiredInputs.description: List of request headers to be used with the REST request

properties.name: headerExpression
properties.description: Header value used for the HTTP request. Can be a constant value or an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: queryParams
requiredInputs.description: List of query parameters for the request URL

properties.name: parameterExpression
properties.description: Parameter value used for the HTTP request. It has to be an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: inputExpression
requiredInputs.description: Provide a simple expression to resolve the body of the HTTP request (e.g getVariable('requestDetails')). Use this ONLY for simple variable references or expressions without multi-line logic. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: inputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to compute or transform the body of the HTTP request. Use this when the input requires multi-line logic, variable manipulation, control flow, or complex transformations. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: outputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to process the response from the server (e.g handle status code and throw exceptions). The returned object will be available in a `response` variable with response.statusLine.statusCode, response.request.uri and response.entity available directly without any additional parsing

generatedOutputs.name: statusCode
generatedOutputs.description: HTTP status code returned by the service

components.name: scriptTask
components.description: A task that is performed based on scripted logic within the process
components.usage: Use script tasks when a task in the process flow requires custom logic or algorithmic processing. It is suitable when the logic can be localized within the process (i.e. does not require external data or systems, which is where a service task is more appropriate). It allows you to define Groovy script scripts to perform specific actions or calculations within the process.

requiredInputs.name: script
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script code to execute

components.name: callActivity
components.description: A task that allows the current process to call another process from within its execution.
components.usage: Use call activity tasks to call another BPMN process by id. It should only be used if an id to the external process is provided.

requiredInputs.name: calledElement
requiredInputs.description: The process id to be called

requiredInputs.name: inputMapping
requiredInputs.description: Variables to be sent to Called Element (the external process) as payload data. E.g, to send payload.myVariable, source expression should be  getVariable('myVariable')  and target should be payload.someVariable. payload.someVariable is then accessible in the external process (the called element)

properties.name: source
properties.description: The source of the data to send to the external process, e.g. payload.myVariable

properties.name: sourceExpression
properties.description: The source expression to send to the external process, e.g.  getVariable('myVariable')

properties.name: target
properties.description: The target data on the external process that captures the data sent from the current process, e.g. payload.someVariable

requiredInputs.name: outputMapping
requiredInputs.description: Variable to be received back from the external process call (the called element). E.g, to use payload.myVariable from the external process, the source expression should be  getVariable('myVariable') . Keep the target as a variable that can be used in this this BPMN. The target variable is directly accessible and can be stored onto payload by persisting in a script task by using `payload.foo = targetVariable.`

properties.name: source
properties.description: The source of the data coming from the external process, e.g. payload.myVariable

properties.name: sourceExpression
properties.description: The source expression coming from the external process, e.g.  getVariable('myVariable')

properties.name: target
properties.description: The target data from the external process that captures the data from the external process to be used in the current process, e.g. targetVariable

requiredInputs.name: businessKey
requiredInputs.description: A boolean expression which gives the user search capabilities for the child process based on the business key. Is set to true by default.

components.name: manualTask
components.description: A task that should be used when a series of manual actions are to be performed external to the process by humans or to be used as a fallback when other bpmn components nodes do not fulfil the request
components.usage: Use manual tasks when the actions require human intervention in external systems outside the process or when explicitly mentioned as a manual task. It can also be used a fallback when other bpmn component nodes do not fulfil the request as a last resort.

components.name: businessRuleTask
components.description: A task that executes a business rule or decision logic
components.usage: Use business rule tasks when a task in the process flow involves executing business rules or decision logic. It allows you to define and execute business rules or decision tables to determine the flow of the process based on certain conditions or criteria.

requiredInputs.name: executionEngine
requiredInputs.description: Execution engine for rule evaluation

requiredInputs.name: applicationId
requiredInputs.description: ID of the Application

requiredInputs.name: ruleName
requiredInputs.description: Rule Name of the rule to be executed

requiredInputs.name: ruleVersion
requiredInputs.description: Rule Version of the rule to be executed

requiredInputs.name: factTypesExpression
requiredInputs.description: Expression to be used to resolve the FactTypes of the rule. Specify either an FactTypes Expression or a FactTypes Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: factTypesScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to resolve the FactTypes of the rule. Specify either an FactTypes Expression or a FactTypes Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: metadataExpression
requiredInputs.description: Expression to be used to resolve the Metadata of the rule. Specify either an Metadata Expression or a Metadata Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: metadataScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to resolve the Metadata of the rule. Specify either an Metadata Expression or a Metadata Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: outputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to process the response from the server (e.g handle status code or throw exceptions). The response object will be available in a `response` variable with response.statusLine.statusCode, response.request.uri and response.entity

components.name: sendTask
components.description: A task that sends a message or signal to another process participant
components.usage: Use send tasks when a task in the process flow involves sending a message or signal to another process participant or external system. It initiates communication or triggers actions in other parts of the process or external systems.

requiredInputs.name: serviceUrl
requiredInputs.description: Direct HTTP/HTTPS URL of the target service (e.g., https://api.example.com). Use this when the service endpoint is known and accessible via a direct URL

requiredInputs.name: uriPath
requiredInputs.description: Specific URI path to append to the location identifier

requiredInputs.name: httpMethod
requiredInputs.description: HTTP Method of the request to be invoked on the REST service called by this task

requiredInputs.name: headers
requiredInputs.description: List of request headers to be used with the REST request

properties.name: headerExpression
properties.description: Header value used for the HTTP request. Can be a constant value or an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: queryParams
requiredInputs.description: List of query parameters for the request URL

properties.name: parameterExpression
properties.description: Parameter value used for the HTTP request. It has to be an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: inputExpression
requiredInputs.description: Provide a simple expression to resolve the body of the HTTP request (e.g getVariable('requestDetails')). Use this ONLY for simple variable references or expressions without multi-line logic. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: inputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to compute or transform the body of the HTTP request. Use this when the input requires multi-line logic, variable manipulation, control flow, or complex transformations. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: outputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to process the response from the server (e.g handle status code and throw exceptions). The response object will be available in a `response` variable with response.statusLine.statusCode, response.request.uri and response.entity

components.name: receiveTask
components.description: A task that waits to receive a message or signal from another process participant.
components.usage: Use receive tasks when a task in the process flow waits to receive a message or signal from another process participant or external system. It typically represents a waiting state until the expected message or signal is received.

requiredInputs.name: messageId
requiredInputs.description: ID of a message to listen for

requiredInputs.name: availabilityRuleScript
requiredInputs.description: A Groovy script that specifies control of who can call this Receive Task

components.name: startEvent
components.description: Represents the beginning of a process flow.
components.usage: Place at the start of the process flow to indicate where it begins. Can have triggers like message, timer, or signal.  Only one per process

components.name: endEvent
components.description: Denotes the completion of a process flow.
components.usage: Place at the end of the process flow to indicate where it ends. Can have outcomes like message, error, or termination. At least one required per process

components.name: exclusiveGateway
components.description: Allows branching based on a condition or merging from multiple paths
components.usage: Use when the process flow can branch to multiple nodes, but ONLY ONE of the paths can be followed. Each outgoing connection flow has a condition which must be met for the process to take that path. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways

requiredInputs.name: default
requiredInputs.description: Identifier of a default target node if no conditions are met

requiredInputs.name: conditions
requiredInputs.description: List of conditions for each outgoing path. Each condition includes the target node identifier and the condition expression to evaluate. Merge gateways with one outgoing path can have empty condition expression

properties.name: targetNodeId
properties.description: Identifier of the target node for this condition

properties.name: conditionExpression
properties.description: Boolean expression used to evaluate whether this path should be taken

components.name: inclusiveGateway
components.description: Allows branching based on a condition or merging from multiple paths
components.usage: Use when the process flow can branch to multiple nodes, and MULTIPLE paths can be followed simultaneously. Each outgoing connection flow has a condition which must be met for the process to take that path. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways.

requiredInputs.name: default
requiredInputs.description: Identifier of a default target node if no conditions are met.

requiredInputs.name: conditions
requiredInputs.description: List of conditions for each outgoing path. Each condition includes the target node identifier and the condition expression to evaluate

properties.name: targetNodeId
properties.description: Identifier of the target node for this condition

properties.name: conditionExpression
properties.description: Boolean expression used to evaluate whether this path should be taken

components.name: parallelGateway
components.description: Allows diverging into, or converging from, multiple parallel paths
components.usage: Use when the process flow should split into multiple parallel paths or merge from multiple parallel paths simultaneously. All outgoing sequence flows are followed in parallel, and all incoming sequence flows must complete before proceeding. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways

components.name: eventBasedGateway
components.description: Allows pausing the process flow and waiting until a subsequent catching event is triggered. At that point, the process proceeds.
components.usage: Use whenever a workflow is required to wait for two or more events at the same time, for instance a message to be received or the passage of time to reach a certain point. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways

components.name: processConfig
components.description: Use this node to represent a configuration of the process. This node has no effect besides documentation. It should not have any outputs or connections to other nodes as it will not be rendered as a node in the executable model
components.usage: Use this node to represent a configuration of the process. This node has no effect besides documentation. It should not have any outputs or connections to other nodes as it will not be rendered as a node in the executable model.

requiredInputs.name: processId
requiredInputs.description: Unique identifier for the process instance

requiredInputs.name: processName
requiredInputs.description: Name of the process appearing to the user. This should contain fixed, contextual information to allow instances of a process to be distinguished

requiredInputs.name: processDescription
requiredInputs.description: Name of the process appearing to the user. This should contain fixed, contextual information to allow instances of a process to be distinguished

requiredInputs.name: sourceSystemName
requiredInputs.description: Source system generated this process

requiredInputs.name: processPriority
requiredInputs.description: Priority level of the process.

requiredInputs.name: processDeadline
requiredInputs.description: Expected completion date and time for the process in date format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) or  duration (e.g. P{days}DT{hours}H{minutes}M)

requiredInputs.name: maximumActiveProcesses
requiredInputs.description: Maximum number of active processes allowed before throttling
